digest.component_or_area: store lock holder naming and timeout reporting
propositions: When a compaction sweep holds the store write lock, blocked sessions see only a bare pid without context about what operation holds it or whether it is safe to interrupt
The sweep's safety property (skipped sweep is a no-op; events stay live for next trigger) is already known to code but not communicated to operators attempting to resolve lock contention

Lock timeout messages should label the holder as a compaction sweep operation via an ambient operation_label contextvar that appends op=compact-sweep to the v2 lock stamp without modifying acquisition call sites
The LockTimeout error message should include a remedy statement for known interruptible operations like compact-sweep, stating the operation can be safely interrupted without data loss
The operation label mechanism must preserve backward compatibility by keeping the stamp colon-free and letting _parse_v2_stamp ignore unknown fields
An unlabelled (ordinary writer) lock holder must render identically to the current format, and staleness/reclamation logic must be blind to the operation label
